name: Phylogeny reconstruction benchmark
description: There are a lot of algorithms and programs for reconstruction of phylogeny of a set of proteins basing on multiple sequence alignment. Many programs allow users to choose a number of parameters, for example, a model for maximum likelihood programs. Different programs and different parameters often produce different results. However at the moment all published benchmarks for evaluation of relative accuracy of programs or different choices of parameters are based on simulated sequences. The aim of the present work is to create a benchmark that allows a comparison of phylogenetic programs on large sets of alignments of natural protein sequences.
reputation: Niche academic benchmark used within the computational phylogenetics community for method comparison, not widely adopted outside phylogenomics specialists.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; results highly sensitive to alignment quality, model choice, and the chosen tree-distance metric; limited clean ground-truth trees for large natural datasets.
